name: Backend performance
description: Server-side query and I/O shape on request and job paths: N+1 queries, unbounded reads, serial awaits, missing indexes, heavy server-rendered fetches and absent caches. Counted sites, not timings; client rendering stays with the built-in performance lens.

fields.label: N+1 queries
fields.description: A query or remote call issued inside a loop over rows on a request or job path.

fields.label: Unbounded queries
fields.description: List endpoints or exports that read every row, with no limit or pagination.

fields.label: Serial awaits
fields.description: Independent I/O awaited one after another on a request path.

fields.label: Missing indexes
fields.description: Columns filtered, joined or sorted on a hot path with no index in the migrations or schema.

fields.label: Heavy render fetches
fields.description: Server-rendered pages or components that fetch unbounded or wide data to render a small view.

fields.label: Uncached hot reads
fields.description: Hot read paths for slow-changing data recomputed on every request with no cache.

rules.reason: {unboundedQueries} list reads have no limit or pagination
{heavyRenderFetches} pages fetch unbounded data to render
{sequentialAwaits} request paths await independent I/O in series
{cacheAbsent} hot reads of slow-changing data are uncached

scan.instructions: Judge the server side of the context: request handlers, server-rendered pages, jobs and the data access they call. Client rendering belongs to the built-in performance lens. Evidence rules - a finding that breaks one is not counted: (1) each finding names file:line, the reachable entry point (route, page, job) and one sentence on why that path is hot or user-facing; no file:line, no count. (2) Count only shipped code: never tests, seeds, one-off scripts, dead code. (3) Before counting, try to refute it: look for the include, batch loader, pagination wrapper, index or cache that already covers the site; it counts only if you can point to the file:line where it is configured. (4) One root cause is one finding listing every entry it reaches. (5) Do not estimate milliseconds or row counts you have not read; this lens counts sites, and a probe measures time. Write 'unverified' for any table size you assume. (6) Per finding suggest a tier 0-3 and a risk_class (usually perf; data when a query can time out a money path) per lens-scan references/triage.md - unbounded reads on hot endpoints are tier 1, N+1 on cold paths tier 2. (7) A context with no server code or data access is not applicable, with a one-line reason; 0 means judged and clean. Doubtful sites go under 'unconfirmed' and never raise a count. Fields: nPlusOne - a query or remote call inside a loop over rows: await prisma.x.findUnique in a for/map, EF Core lazy navigation without Include, Django access without select_related/prefetch_related, JPA lazy collections without a fetch join; show the loop and the query. unboundedQueries - list endpoints or exports reading all rows: findMany() with no take, ToList() on a DbSet with no Take, Model.objects.all() serialized whole, findAll() with no Pageable, SELECT without LIMIT; a table you can show is bounded by design (a fixed lookup) is not a finding. sequentialAwaits - two or more awaits in series where neither uses the other's result and Promise.all, Task.WhenAll, asyncio.gather or CompletableFuture.allOf would apply; show they are independent. missingIndexes - a column filtered, joined or ordered on a hot path with no index in the schema (Prisma @@index, EF HasIndex, Django db_index or Meta.indexes, JPA @Index, CREATE INDEX); primary keys and unique constraints count as indexes; name the query and the schema file you checked. heavyRenderFetches - server components, getServerSideProps, loaders, Razor pages or templates fetching every row or every column to render a small view. cacheAbsent - a hot read of slow-changing data (reference lists, exchange rates, settings, dashboard aggregates) recomputed per request with no cache (revalidate or unstable_cache, IMemoryCache or output cache, Django cache, Spring @Cacheable, Redis); count only when you can say why the data changes slowly.
